The Royal Gallery sits adjacent to the Royal Library, just beyond the verdant interior garden of Stormwind Keep. The hall houses statues of towering figures who shaped the realm: King Llane Wrynn, the fallen ruler of Stormwind; Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras; and Mara Fordragon, ancestor of the current Regent. It serves as both a private museum of noble heritage and a quiet retreat for courtly visitors like Lady Dena Kennedy.

Tucked deep within the stone wing of Stormwind Keep, the Royal Library preserves the collective memory, chronicle scrolls, and treatises of the kingdom. Under the watchful eye of Head Librarian Milton Sheaf, its shelves hold crucial records of ancient wars, lost legends, and the realms beyond the sea.

While Stormwind Keep bristles with armored guards and courtly intrigue, its Royal Library offers an island of scholarly quiet. Overseen by Milton Sheaf, the hall serves as the premier archive of southern human history, preserving surviving texts from before the First War alongside recent military chronicles and recovered tomes. Alliance scholars, priests, and travelers are free to browse its open treatises, which cover everything from the formation of the original Alliance of Lordaeron to the recent emergence of Thrall's Horde in Kalimdor.

The library has not always remained unmolested by outside conflicts. Following the Second War, the dangerous Book of Medivh was stored within its vaults, drawing Alterac infiltrators and death knights sent by Ner'zhul in a brazen castle raid.

The Royal Quarter is the secluded seat of power within the Undercity, serving as the throne room for Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Here, the Banshee Queen directs the Forsaken alongside her dreadlord enforcer, Varimathras, guarded by an elite cohort of Royal Dreadguards.
The Seat of the Dark Lady

Tucked away behind towering archways and shadowed corridors, the Royal Quarter—also known as the Hall of the Dark Lady—is the political and military nerve center of the Forsaken. Sylvanas Windrunner holds court in this cavernous subterranean chamber, plotting the survival of her free-willed undead and the destruction of the Scourge. Heavily armored Royal Dreadguards stand vigil along the dais, ensuring that uninvited guests and would-be assassins never reach their queen.

Standing beside the Dark Lady is the nathrezim Varimathras, an unexpected and uneasy fixture in the heart of the Undercity. After siding with Sylvanas during the civil war in the ruins of Lordaeron to save his own life, the dreadlord pledged loyalty to her cause. From the Royal Quarter, he commands deathstalkers and coordinates defensive operations across the realm. While his tactical cunning serves the Forsaken well, his demonic nature leaves many Horde allies wary of his true allegiances.

The Ruined Reaches comprise the treacherous southern coastline of Azshara near the border with Durotar. Marked by crumbling ancient ruins, shattered shipwrecks, and jagged shallows, these beaches are overrun by aggressive shoreline predators. Amid the desolation, a small gnomish outpost perches high on a cliffside above the surf.

Stretching along the southern borders of Azshara just north of Durotar, the Ruined Reaches are a maze of rocky inlets, cliff faces, and debris-strewn sand. Like the Jagged Reef further north, hidden shallows make maritime travel extremely hazardous, leaving numerous ruined vessels broken along the shore. The waters and beaches teem with hostile wildlife, including territorial murlocs, vicious hydras, and armored makrura, making overland transit just as dangerous as navigating the surf.

Perched upon a western cliff overlooking the beaches sits an unexpected pocket of tinker civilization: a gnomish workshop accessible via a steep trail from Azshara's mainland. Run by Blimo and Jubie Gadgetspring, this outpost offers engineering components and general trade goods to passing adventurers. The interior features an elevator ascending to private quarters with three beds, though who—if anyone—claims the third bunk remains a quiet domestic mystery.

The Ruins of Aboraz are ancient Gurubashi stone ruins nestled along the southeastern cliffs of Stranglethorn Vale. Once part of the sprawling jungle troll empire, the crumbling terraces now serve as the secluded redoubt for the renegade witch doctor Zanzil the Outcast and his mind-addled thralls.

Perched on the bluffs southeast of the Ruins of Jubuwal and south of the Crystalvein Mine, the weathered masonry of Aboraz has been transformed into an alchemical testing ground. Zanzil the Outcast was banished by the local tribes and the mainlanders alike, retreating here to brew potent mind-altering concoctions and toxic elixirs. Within the stone courtyards, Zanzil exerts total control over an unsettling menagerie of servitors, including shambling undead ghouls, corrupted troll thralls, and even co-opted coastal naga.

Zanzil's strange potions do not simply poison the body—they shatter the will. Among the lost souls pacing the terraces is the enthralled Darkspear youth Yenniku, whose mind remains locked under Zanzil's sorcery. The snow-covered Ruins of Alterac are all that remain of Alterac City, once the proud mountain capital of the Kingdom of Alterac. Cast out of the Alliance and put under martial law after King Aiden Perenolde's treason during the Second War, the shattered stronghold is now overrun by the brutish Crushridge ogres.

Alterac was once an independent human realm carved out of the old Arathor empire, perched high on the trade routes through the mountains. During the Second War, fearing destruction at the hands of the invading Old Horde, King Aiden Perenolde secretly struck a pact with the orcs. When the betrayal was uncovered following the fighting at Caer Darrow, the Alliance of Lordaeron retaliated swiftly. King Terenas Menethil II put the city under martial law and deposed Perenolde. The grand fortifications, church, and palace fell into disrepair as the populace fled or turned to outlawry.

While surviving Alteraci nobles and rogue soldiers formed the Syndicate to wage guerrilla campaigns from towns like Strahnbrad, they lost their ancestral capital entirely. Today, the Crushridge ogres under Mug'thol dwell among the broken ramparts, palace halls, and wrecked ballistae. Neither the Syndicate nor the human defenders of Southshore have managed to reclaim the fallen city, leaving its crumbling towers and abandoned vaults as dangerous territory for treasure hunters and scavengers.

Once the agricultural hub and grain distribution center of northern Lordaeron, the Ruins of Andorhal now lie at the heart of the Western Plaguelands as a devastated Necropolis stronghold. Under the dominion of the lich Araj the Summoner, the shattered township crawls with legions of undead abominations, ghouls, and wraiths.

Andorhal was the initial staging ground for the plague of undeath in Lordaeron, where grain tainted by the Cult of the Damned was packed and distributed across the human kingdom. Today, the ruined city serves as a sprawling bastion of the Scourge in the Western Plaguelands. Araj the Summoner presides over the center of the ruins, flanked by ghouls, skeletal horrors, and towering flesh golems. Scouting parties of the Scarlet Crusade periodically probe the city's outskirts, but the Scourge maintains iron control over the shattered streets.

Beyond the physical presence of the undead, Andorhal suffers from peculiar temporal anomalies. The town hall clock and discarded pocket watches scattered through the streets remain perpetually stopped at three o'clock. The bronze dragon Chromie, sheltering in the inn on the edge of the ruins, investigates temporal parasites nesting within the grain silos. Scourge forces appear to be meddling with the flow of time itself, attempting to alter the timeline of the city's tragic downfall.

The Ruins of Arkkoran comprise the shattered, wave-battered stonework of an ancient night elven sanctuary along the rugged coast of Azshara. Named after the ancient sea giant Arkkoroc who watches over these waters, the site lies submerged in tidepools and roamed by coastal beasts.

Stretching along the jagged coast of Azshara, the Ruins of Arkkoran are all that remain of the outer perimeters of an ancient night elven temple complex. Long before the shores broke apart in the Great Sundering, highborne worshippers built stone monuments here by the sea. Today, salt spray and centuries of erosion have reduced the proud marble to crumbling plinths and collapsed walls. The surrounding tidal shallows are now home to aggressive makrura, snapdragons, and tidal elementals, while the deep waters nearby remain under the watchful eye of the primordial sea giant Arkkoroc.

The Ruins of Constellas are the shattered remnants of an ancient night elf settlement in Felwood, nestled near the roots of Mount Hyjal. Today, the once-sacred grounds are overrun by the Jadefire satyrs, who have violently profaned the settlement's moonwell with demonic fel magic.

The classical stone arches and crumbling plazas of Constellas reveal that this was once an idyllic night elven community. During the Third War, the Burning Legion's march through Felwood shattered the haven, leaving it exposed to lingering demonic corruption. Now, the foul Jadefire satyrs hold dominion over the stones. Led by Xavathras, they actively tend to a defiled moonwell, transforming pure waters into a font of noxious fel power on behalf of their master, Lord Xavaric.

The defilement of Constellas has provoked active resistance from Kalimdor's defenders. Druidic Emerald Bearkin battle the satyrs throughout the ruins in an attempt to reclaim the forest, while night elven investigators observe from a nearby camp to the southeast. To protect their foul rituals and prevent intruders from reaching Xavathras, the satyrs have sealed the deeper pathways into the ruins behind an impenetrable wall of magical fire.

The Ruins of Eldarath are the shattered remains of a pre-Sundering Highborne city perched along the rocky bluffs of Azshara. Once a bastion of Kaldorei arcane scholarship, its fallen plazas and crumbling temples are now overrun by hostile naga. Scholars and adventurers brave the dangerous coastal ruins searching for inscribed tablets and forgotten relics of the ancient past.

Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, Eldarath was a flourishing night elven city. Renowned Highborne mages gathered here, carving their deepest arcane insights and fundamental magical rules into grand stone tablets left in public squares for their peers to study. During the apocalyptic War of the Ancients, the city became a battlefield between the Kaldorei Resistance and the demonic Burning Legion before the Sundering dropped much of Eldarath into the Bay of Storms. The portions that survived along the eastern cliffs have sat shunned by modern night elves for millennia, slowly claimed by creeping salt spray and ivy.

In recent times, vicious naga have emerged from the sea to seize the shattered streets of Eldarath, commanded by warlords lurking within nearby sanctuaries like the Temple of Zin-Malor. Despite the danger posed by the serpents, the ruins remain an irresistible lure for outsiders. The Explorers' League has dispatched Alliance adventurers into the broken courtyards to take rubbings of Eldarath's ancient arcane tablets. Whispers of lost treasures and lingering magical energy also drew the blue dragon Azuregos to the surrounding wilderness, further confirming that secrets of immense power still sleep beneath the ruins' cracked flagstones.
